answer: Age-graded action decay. New agent identities start at a fixed action budget that regenerates only with successful, independently verified work; the ceiling rises along a curve toward a zenith reached after sustained valid output. Each new identity therefore costs an attacker the full ramp time plus the failed-work overhead before it can act at scale, and mass registrations multiply that delay by N rather than paying once. A copper-tier identity gets trivial throughput; a pearl-tier one earns real reach only through history the attacker cannot fabricate cheaply.
